text.headline: Crypto regulation and flows: Bitcoin +2.1%, Ether +3.8%
text.tone: Markets sent mixed signals as digital assets gained on regulatory news while rising yields weighed on precious metals and industrial commodities.
lead: The week begins with digital assets showing resilience following a session of mixed signals across global asset classes. On Friday, US large caps fell −0.6% as the VIX volatility index rose +3.2%, while Treasury yields climbed across the curve, with the 10-year yield reaching 5.15%. However, the new week has seen a divergence in sentiment, as [[crypto|Bitcoin]] rose +2.1% to $65,447 and Ether climbed +3.8% to $1,835, contrasting with a broader retreat in commodities and traditional equities.

The primary driver for digital assets appears to be a confirmed theme of crypto regulation and flows. While some local authorities are moving to ban cryptocurrency kiosks due to fraud concerns, institutional interest remains a stabilizing force, as seen in reports of major university endowments maintaining steady positions in spot ETFs. In the broader market, rising US yields, including a +5 bp move in the 10-year, drew capital toward the dollar, putting pressure on the [[crypto|EUR/USD]], which fell −0.3% to 1.1014.

The upward move in yields has spread quickly to the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]], where gold fell −0.7% to $3,859. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets, a relationship that also saw silver drop −4.5% to $46.91. This weakness extended to industrial metals, with platinum falling −2.8% and copper down −0.7%, suggesting softer expectations for manufacturing demand. Meanwhile, [[islamic|Shariah-compliant shares]] mirrored the wider equity market, with the EB Shariah US 100 index declining −0.7%.

These moves suggest a market grappling with high interest rates even as specific sectors like digital finance find idiosyncratic support. The current regime of mixed signals would be confirmed if yields remain elevated while corporate credit spreads stay calm, as noted in the latest [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]]. Conversely, a sharp reversal in the dollar would contradict the current trend. Readers can explore how these shifting yields impact long-term valuations on our [[outlook|Market Outlook]] page.

briefs.markets: US yields rose across the curve on Friday, with the 30-year yield reaching 5.47%, creating a headwind for [[markets|equities]] as the EB US 100 fell −0.6%.
briefs.energy: In the latest data from November 11, Brent crude rose +2.2% to $92.14, though the [[energy|Energy Terminal]] shows significant monthly volatility persists.
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin and Ether gained +2.1% and +3.8% respectively, outperforming a strengthening dollar which saw the [[crypto|EUR/USD]] drop to 1.1014.
briefs.metals: Precious metals faced selling pressure as yields rose, with silver falling a notable −4.5% to $46.91 on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]].
briefs.estate: The [[estate|Estate Index]] shows a stark geographic divide, with house prices rising +33.7% in Moldova while falling −6.3% in China.
briefs.corporate: The [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]] identifies a risk-on regime for credit, with APA Corporation earning a top EB Score of 89.
briefs.outlook: The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] for Q4 remains cautious, as semiconductors have fallen −24.8% since the quarter began amid a broader risk-off environment.
briefs.islamic: The EB Shariah US 100 fell −0.7% to 116.90, though [[islamic|Islamic Investment]] returns of +14.1% YTD continue to outperform the broader market.

watch: US Treasury yield movements following Friday's climb, as the 10-year yield at 5.15% continues to dictate the direction of the dollar and non-yielding precious metals.
Institutional crypto flow data, as Bitcoin and Ether test resistance levels amid a confirmed regulatory theme and steady ETF holdings by major institutional players.
Industrial metal price action, specifically silver and platinum, for further clues on global manufacturing demand as both assets showed notable weakness in the latest session.
